message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | ~1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g/L (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C |
| | Specific heat capacity | 14.304 J/(mol·K) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L/mol |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –72.8 kJ/mol |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ/mol |
| | Acidic strength | Strong acid when protonated (H⁺) |
| | Basicity | Weak base as hydride (H⁻) |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water or oxides |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Solubility in water | 0.00018 mol/L (very low) |
| | Ability to form hydrogen bonds | Yes (in water, alcohols, etc.) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Deuterium (²H) | Heavy hydrogen; used in NMR, D₂O (“heavy water”) |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive; used in radiolabeling, fusion research |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel cell technology | Proton exchange membrane fuel cells |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Space & aviation | Rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen) |
| | Medical imaging | Deuterium labeling in NMR spectroscopy |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen storage, metal hydrides |
| | Nuclear fusion research | Deuterium–tritium fusion in tokamaks |
| **Safety & Handling** | Explosion limits in air | Lower limit 4 %, upper limit 75 % |
| | Storage pressure | Up to 700 bar for compressed gas; cryogenic liquid at –253 °C |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; inhalation can cause hypoxia due to displacement of oxygen |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, and no neutrons in its most common isotope (protium).
- It is a **colorless, odorless, tasteless gas** that is extremely light and highly flammable.
- Its **chemical behavior** is dominated by its ability to donate or accept a proton, forming acids (H⁺) or hydrides (H⁻).
- **Isotopic variants** (deuterium, tritium) give hydrogen unique roles in scientific research and energy applications.
- **Safety**: handle with care—store under high pressure or cryogenic conditions, keep away from ignition sources, and monitor for oxygen displacement in confined spaces.
